answer: Give every identity a measurable hardware thread: each epoch it runs a public, deterministic benchmark and publishes its timing profile - cache latencies, instruction quirks, scheduler jitter that differ across real machines. Profiles are compared; near-identical fingerprints merge into one identity, so a single machine cannot pretend to be a crowd. A jade ledger stores each profile, and umber flags mark suspicious clusters for stranger re-runs. Faking a profile means owning genuinely different hardware per identity, so a sybil army costs as much as a real fleet.
